title: Self-Registration Portal Storm Detection and Bot-Onboarding Defense
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Does not constitute legal, regulatory, or executive attestation for 'Self-Registration Portal Storm Detection and Bot-Onboarding Defense'. Does not cover entities explicitly scoped out in operational_exceptions.csv. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-17.1.52).
evidence: Saved search uc_17_1_52_self_registration_portal_storm_detection, dashboard panel tied to this UC, weekly CSV export archived to index=evidence with change-ticket reference, and git-tracked lookup baselines referenced in the search.

compliance.assurance_rationale: PCI 8.5.1 covers MFA / strong auth controls.
compliance.controlObjective: Strong auth control on guest portal.

compliance.assurance_rationale: Art.21(2)(b) — incident handling. Bot-onboarding storms qualify as incidents.
AC-2(11) (Usage Conditions) — abnormal-onboarding detection evidences usage-condition monitoring.
A.5.16 (Identity management) — guest identity creation audit.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Script 110 self-registrations from 2 source IPs. UC-17.1.52 fires with `suspicious=likely_bot` for the `gmail.com` domain.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run 10 organic self-registrations from various IPs. UC-17.1.52 returns `suspicious=normal`.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *Self-Registration Portal* category — codes `86100` (self-registration started), `86101` (self-registration completed), `86102` (self-registration failed), `86103` (self-registration captcha failed), `86104` (self-registration rate-limit), `86110` (email validation failure), `86120` (mass self-registration anomaly). Fields: `guest_user`, `email_domain`, `client_ip`, `mac_address`, `failed_reason`.
spl:
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (86100, 86101, 86102, 86104, 86110)
| stats count, dc(guest_user) as unique_users, dc(client_ip) as unique_ips, dc(mac_address) as unique_macs by email_domain
| eval suspicious = case(
    unique_users > 100 AND unique_ips < 5, "likely_bot",
    unique_users > 50 AND unique_macs/unique_users < 0.5, "likely_bot",
    count > 500, "possible_storm",
    true(), "normal")
| where suspicious != "normal"
description: Detects self-registration portal storms and bot-driven onboarding patterns — characterised by many user creations from few source IPs or MACs.
value: Self-registration portals are a common attack target. Botnets attempt to create thousands of accounts to exhaust IP pools, evade rate-limiting, or onboard malicious devices. Detecting the storm in real-time enables CAPTCHA hardening, IP allow-listing, or temporary portal disable.
implementation: Confirm *Self-Registration Portal* category at INFO. Schedule every 5 min, search window `-15m@m to @m`, trigger on count > 0, throttle suppression on `email_domain` for 30 min.
visualization: (1) Single value: storm signal (red if `suspicious != normal`). (2) Map: client_ip geographic distribution. (3) Top-N: domains.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• ISE Self-Registration portal enabled.
• `event_calendar.csv` for context.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable *Self-Registration Portal* category at INFO.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field. Schedule every 5 min.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — Self-Reg Storm":
• Storm signal tile.
• Geographic distribution.
• Top-N domains.

Alerting: PagerDuty high on `likely_bot`.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **CAPTCHA still bypassed** — Tune CAPTCHA settings on the portal.
• **Storm persists after IP block** — Attack uses VPN; block by user-agent or behavioural pattern.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`email_domain, suspicious, unique_ips, unique_users`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: A guest sign-up page on the network — like a sign-in sheet at a hotel — can be abused by automated programs creating fake guest accounts. We watch for many sign-ups from few computers and ring the bell when the pattern looks like a bot.
